name: ava

schema.description: Configuration Schema for the JavaScript test runner AVA

files.description: An array of glob patterns to select test files. Files with an underscore prefix are ignored. By default only selects files with `cjs`, `mjs` & `js` extensions, even if the pattern matches other files. Specify `extensions` to allow other file extensions

ignoredByWatcher.description: An array of glob patterns to match files that, even if changed, are ignored by the watcher

match.description: Not typically useful in the `package.json` configuration, but equivalent to specifying `--match` on the CLI

cache.description: Defaults to `true` to cache compiled files under `node_modules/.cache/ava.` If `false`, files are cached in a temporary directory instead

concurrency.description: Max number of test files running at the same time (default: CPU cores)

workerThreads.description: Use worker threads to run tests (enabled by default). If `false`, tests will run in child processes

failFast.description: Stop running further tests once a test fails

failWithoutAssertions.description: If `false`, does not fail a test if it doesn't run assertions

environmentVariables.title: environment variables
environmentVariables.description: Specifies environment variables to be made available to the tests. The environment variables defined here override the ones from `process.env`

serial.description: if `true`, prevents parallel execution of tests within a file

verbose.description: If `true`, enables verbose output (though currently non-verbose output is not supported)

snapshotDir.description: Specifies a fixed location for storing snapshot files. Use this if your snapshots are ending up in the wrong location

extensions.description: Extensions of test files. Setting this overrides the default `["cjs", "mjs", "js"]` value, so make sure to include those extensions in the list. Experimentally you can configure how files are loaded

require.description: Extra modules to require before tests are run. Modules are required in the worker processes

timeout.description: Timeouts in AVA behave differently than in other test frameworks. AVA resets a timer after each test, forcing tests to quit if no new test results were received within the specified timeout. This can be used to handle stalled tests. See our timeout documentation for more options

nodeArguments.description: Configure Node.js arguments used to launch worker processes

typescript.title: configuration
typescript.description: Configures @ava/typescript for projects that precompile TypeScript. Alternatively, you can use `ts-node` to do live testing without transpiling, in which case you shouldn't use the `typescript` property

extensions.description: You can configure AVA to recognize additional file extensions as TypeScript (e.g., `["ts", "tsx"]` to add partial JSX support). Note that the preserve mode for JSX is not (yet) supported. See also AVA's `extensions` object

rewritePaths.title: paths
rewritePaths.description: AVA searches your entire project for `*.js`, `*.cjs`, `*.mjs` and `*.ts` files (or other extensions you've configured). It will ignore such files found in the `rewritePaths` targets (e.g. `build/`). If you use more specific paths, for instance `build/main/`, you may need to change AVA's `files` configuration to ignore other directories. Paths are relative to your project directory

compile.description: If `false`, AVA will assume you have already compiled your project. If set to `'tsc'`, AVA will run the TypeScript compiler before running your tests. This can be inefficient when using AVA in watch mode

schema.title: AVA Config Schema

description:
The test suite is set up to run any JavaScript files under `test/**/*.js` as well as CommonJS modules under `src/**/*.cjs`, while the watcher will ignore changes in the `dist/**` and `node_modules/**` directories. Only the tests matching the pattern `test/unit/**` will be selected when a match filter is applied. Caching is enabled, and up to four test files may run concurrently, using worker threads for execution. The runner will not stop on the first failure (fail‑fast is disabled) and will still enforce that each test contains at least one assertion. Environment variables for the test run are defined as `NODE_ENV=test` and `API_URL=http://localhost:3000`. Tests are allowed to run in parallel within files (serial execution is off), the TAP reporter is disabled, and verbose output is turned on. Snapshot files are stored in `test/__snapshots__`. The allowed file extensions for test discovery are `cjs`, `mjs`, `js` and `ts`, and the only module required before the tests start is `@babel/register`. Each test is given a timeout of 30 seconds, and the Node.js processes that run the workers receive the argument `--experimental-modules`. Parallel builds are utilized.

For TypeScript handling, the configuration recognizes both `.ts` and `.tsx` files as TypeScript sources. AVA is instructed to ignore any files found under `build/` by mapping `build/` to `build/` in the rewrite‑paths setting, and the TypeScript compilation step is disabled, assuming the project is already compiled.
